body: Evergrande was the world's most indebted developer with ~$300 bn of liabilities (incl. presold apartments, supplier IOUs, wealth-management products sold to staff and the public). The stock rallied ~400%+ in 2017 to a peak ~HK$30 (Jul 2017-2018 area) and was suspended at ~HK$0.16 before delisting on 25 Aug 2025. Timeline: Aug 2020 Beijing's 'three red lines' (liability/assets ex-advances <70%, net gearing <100%, cash/short-term debt >1x) -- Evergrande failed all three; Sep 2021 missed payments and WMP protests; Dec 2021 offshore default; Jan 29 2024 Hong Kong court liquidation order; Mar 2024 CSRC found onshore unit Hengda inflated revenue by ~RMB 564 bn in 2019-2020 and fined founder Hui Ka Yan. Visible flags: (1) total liabilities growing faster than sales; heavy reliance on presales and commercial paper to suppliers; (2) perpetual bonds and high-yield offshore USD debt at 10%+; (3) large special dividends paid while highly levered; (4) diversification into EVs, football, bottled water; (5) contract assets/receivables and 'cash' that was restricted; (6) policy shift (three red lines) directly targeting its model. Lesson: when a sovereign changes rules aimed at your leverage model, exit; dividends paid out of borrowed money are a value-destruction signal. Liquidation recoveries for equity ~0.

data.early_signals: failed three red lines; WMP funding; dividends with leverage; diversification; restricted cash
data.lesson: Policy aimed at your leverage = exit; equity in liquidation ~0

title: China Evergrande (2021-2025): leverage in presales
